__reason.src/pages/PaymentRequests.tsx: Iron rule, docs/HANDOFF-english-language-20260827.md §9: audit_logs is evidence and is never translated. The seven lines that stay are the audit reasons this screen writes — reasonOr(reason, ...) at creation, the PAYMENT_REQUEST_ACTION_LABEL table the approver falls back to, and the exceptional-approval reason — all of which travel into p_reason / p_override_reason and land in audit_logs. Translating them would rewrite a ledger entry in a language the ledger was not written in. Everything a person reads on this screen is extracted.
__reason.src/pages/InvoiceDetail.tsx: Iron rule, docs/HANDOFF-english-language-20260827.md §9: audit_logs is evidence and is never translated. The five lines that stay are the audit wording of INVOICE_REVIEW_ACTIONS — each action carries a labelKey the button renders in the reader's language AND an auditLabel that reaches p_reason through reasonOr(). Splitting the two is deliberate: an audit trail whose wording depends on who pressed the button cannot be searched. PaymentRequests.tsx makes the same split for the same reason.
__reason.src/pages/Onboarding.tsx: Two deliberate classes, neither of them copy this feature owns. (1) CATEGORY_SUGGESTIONS[].name is the value WRITTEN TO categories.name, copied byte-for-byte from starter_categories in supabase/seed.sql — the seed inserts "on conflict (org_id, name) do nothing", so a translated value would silently create a second category beside the seeded one. The visible label follows the reader through labelKey; only the stored value stays canonical. (2) The Hebrew words in each FieldSpec aliases[] are what autoMapColumns matches against the HEADER ROW OF AN UPLOADED SPREADSHEET. They are input recognition, not copy: translating them would stop auto-mapping a Hebrew file that maps on the first try today. Every field label that used to sit in the label property was MOVED INTO aliases for exactly that reason, so nothing that used to match stopped matching.
__reason.src/components/document-review/model.ts: The sixteen lines that stay are OCR MATCHING VOCABULARY, not copy, and translating them would break document reading outright. Each array — QUANTITY_KEYS, UNIT_PRICE_KEYS, LINE_TOTAL_KEYS, INVOICE_NUMBER_KEYS, INVOICE_DATE_KEYS, BEFORE_VAT_KEYS, VAT_KEYS, TOTAL_KEYS, SKU_KEYS, BARCODE_KEYS, DESCRIPTION_KEYS, QUANTITY_LINE_KEYS, the credited-invoice keys, PAYMENT_REFERENCE_KEYS and PAYMENT_DATE_KEYS — holds the words a SUPPLIER PRINTED ON PAPER, matched against text the OCR read back. They are inputs the system recognises, in the same class as FieldSpec.aliases in Onboarding.tsx. The English word for each field is already in the same array beside the Hebrew one, so an English invoice matches today; replacing the Hebrew would stop a Hebrew invoice from matching at all. Everything a person READS on this surface — every label table, every confidence grade, every filing-reason sentence, the routing summary and the rule explanation — moved into the dictionary, and this module now takes the translator as an argument because it is pure and cannot hold a hook.

Same split as PaymentRequests.tsx and InvoiceDetail.tsx.
__reason.src/components/document-review/PriceList: Six lines stay, one from each protected class. (1) The regex in guessLineName matches KEY NAMES THE OCR PRODUCED from a Hebrew price list; it is recognition, like the keyword arrays in model.ts. (2) Three unit-of-measure defaults reach products.unit through normalizeUnitInput, and 0001 stores that column in Hebrew — the Hebrew value IS the key, and changing it moves name_match_key and the three-way match with it (see PLAN section 3.2, which keeps units for phase 3 and forbids a data migration). (3) One reasonOr() fallback reaches p_reason and lands in audit_logs. Everything a person reads on this surface is extracted.
